then.text: Practice is Thursday and Saturday. If you ever hear a roof coming off in the Rhondda, that's us.
Four parts at last: first tenor, second tenor, baritone and a proper bass. Four parts and one conductor with a very sore throat.
The eisteddfod pavilion is packed to the rafters. Elwyn raises his baton. For a moment there is no sound at all.
Then forty men breathe in together, and the roof lifts. The Cwm Rhondda goes up through the canvas like a rocket.
Second place! Second! We beat the Treorchy boys by a whisker and a bad key change. Here. Take the medal. It's yours as much as ours.

Bore da. Elwyn Prosser, conductor of the Bethania Male Voice Choir. We've got the National Eisteddfod in a fortnight and we're a quartet short.

I need four voices: a first tenor, a second tenor, a baritone and a bass. I've heard rumours of singers in the bakehouse over the road, in a pub in Merthyr, in the Workmen's Hall at Blaenavon, and underground in Big Pit.
Find them for me. And tell them they won't be paid, but there'll be tea.

rhn_organist.text: Nineteen hymns, six anthems and a Welsh Wedding March. I could play any of them in my sleep, and I have, in the sermon.
A male voice choir needs four parts: first tenor, second tenor, baritone, bass. Miss any one and you can hear the hole in it, like a missing tooth.
